findings.title: Renderer and checker accept different Unicode aliases for new reserved license paths
findings.requirement: SPEC §4 local resources/tool contract and input contract: generated output name collisions are rejected before first write; generated output is checked by actual Python.
findings.reproduction: Keep the representative source, append a second source with path Licenſes/own.txt (U+017F). Renderer returns GENERATED and writes its output; actual checker fails source:1:file because Python casefold maps long s to s while JS toLowerCase does not.
findings.evidence: collision-r2-results.json results[0]; exact generated output retained at collision-r2/output-0
findings.impact: An accepted input produces an artifact rejected by the mandatory next step. The new reserved license namespace is not interpreted consistently.

findings.title: Windows trailing-dot components bypass new reserved output checks
findings.requirement: Input contract: reject file/directory output conflicts; source paths/bytes remain verifiable; SPEC §4 Windows/path support.
findings.reproduction: Append source path licenses./Apache-2.0.txt or LICENSE./source.md to otherwise-valid representative input on Windows. Renderer reports GENERATED and writes output, but actual checker fails path/manifest checks after Windows path normalization.
findings.evidence: collision-r2-results.json results[3..5]; exact generated outputs retained
findings.impact: Input names aliasing new generated file/directory names reach writes and cannot be reliably reopened/verified by the mandatory checker.

observations.title: The checker only proves declared license-file manifest consistency
observations.reproduction: Delete LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/Apache-2.0.txt from a generated bundle, and remove corresponding manifest entries. Actual checker returns PASS/0.
observations.classification: Assurance gap pending scope decision: static checker currently requires only index/theme/js. To claim mandatory license completeness, require these three files and add the self-consistent-manifest negative case.

verified.rawLicenseBytes: MIT and Apache byte-equal to isolated installed package
verified.notice: Original package notice appears as one unmodified tail, with scoped prefix
verified.firstWrite: All tracked content/license/asset read calls precede first mkdir/write in normal renderer run
verified.missingInstalled: All 3 missing assets throw before creating output
verified.inputAndCache: Input and installed bytes unchanged on normal run

regressionTestAssessment: The new tests exercise actual installed copies, raw notice/license/source bytes, real Python, missing installed assets before first write, manifest hashes, and ASCII collisions. They are necessary for real package-boundary failures; the missing Unicode/Windows and self-consistent-manifest cases explain the observed gaps.
